title: Fractional Chromatic Number Bound for Planar Triangle-Free Graphs
statement_text: The fractional chromatic number of $n$-vertex planar triangle-free graphs might be bounded by $3 - 3/(n+1)$.
context_text: Graphs are simple. The fractional chromatic number $\chi_f(G)$ is the minimum of $a/b$ over all positive integers $a\ge b$ such that each vertex can be assigned a $b$-element subset of $\{1,\dots,a\}$ with adjacent vertices receiving disjoint subsets; $\chi_f(G)\le\chi(G)$ and $\alpha(G)\ge|V(G)|/\chi_f(G)$. By Grötzsch's theorem planar triangle-free graphs are 3-colorable, so $\alpha(G)\ge n/3$; Steinberg and Tovey proved $\alpha(G)\ge(n+1)/3$ for every $n$-vertex planar triangle-free graph and described an infinite class of graphs attaining it, and the authors prove that every other $n$-vertex planar triangle-free graph has $\alpha(G)\ge(n+2)/3$. Since a graph with $\alpha=(n+1)/3$ has $\chi_f\ge n/\alpha=3-3/(n+1)$, these results indicate that $\chi_f(G)\le 3-3/(n+1)$ might hold for every $n$-vertex planar triangle-free graph $G$. Dvořák, Sereni and Volec proved this for planar triangle-free graphs of maximum degree at most 4; in general only the weaker bound $3-3/(3n+1)$ is known.
notes: Stated with hedged language ('might be bounded'); the paper presents it as a consequence suggested by its main results together with the known partial result for maximum degree at most 4.
paper_title: Triangle-free planar graphs with the smallest independence number
